question: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize for Literature for which book?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gitanjali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1913, **poet Rabindranath Tagore **was awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature for his collection** Gitanjali,** which was published in London in 1912.
 
• The fact that the prize was handed to an Indian for the first time added to its prominence.
 
• Tagore's literary reputation was cemented by this award. In protest at the 1919 Amritsar Massacre, Tagore surrendered his Knighthood for Services to Literature, which he had received in 1915. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Rabindranath Tagore's Poetry Compilation book is titled** 'Sanchayita.'**
 
• **Gora** is a novel by Rabindranath Tagore set in the 1880s during the British Raj in Calcutta (now Kolkata). It is the fifth and longest of Tagore's twelve books in terms of writing sequence.
 
• **Gitabitan** is a book that contains all 2,232 of Bengali polymath Rabindranath Tagore's songs.
